substantiveDifference: Living-owner agent authority and document-review handoff, rather than remote signing logistics, heir authority or generic title problems.

faq.q: Can a power of attorney be used to sell a Houston house?
faq.a: A suitable power of attorney may authorize an agent to handle a sale. Have a Texas attorney and the closing team review the actual document, property and proposed transaction before relying on it.

faq.q: Is every power of attorney suitable for a house sale?
faq.a: No. Different documents grant different powers. Do not assume a medical, vehicle or other limited authorization permits a real-estate sale.

faq.q: Does signing from another state mean I need a power of attorney?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Ask the closing team about available signing arrangements. How the owner signs and whether an agent has authority are separate questions.

faq.q: Does a cash buyer replace review of the agent's authority?
faq.a: No. Compare the purchase terms separately while the appropriate professionals confirm the authority and closing requirements.
